extracted.intended_audience: students and coaches preparing for math olympiads; contest participants looking for past problems and solutions
extracted.subtask_description: An index page collecting problems and solutions for international and USA math olympiad contests (IMO, USAMO, TST, EGMO, ELMO, etc.), intended as a resource for training and reference. Includes downloadable PDFs/TeX, videos where available, and a personal hardness rating system.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOHS hardness scale
rubrics_metrics.description: The difficulties are rated from 0 to 50 in increments of 5, using a scale I devised called MOHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an index of many problems by the author's opinions on their difficulty and subject. The ratings are the author's personal system (MOHS = 'math olympiad hardness scale') and the document links each problem to corresponding solution threads on AoPS. Use the numeric 0–50 (step 5) scale as an informal difficulty indicator when selecting problems for practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjectivity of difficulty ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: The ratings (and even philosophy) are the author's own personal opinion, rather than some sort of indisputable truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat MOHS ratings as subjective guidance, not absolute measures. The author explicitly disclaims that the scale reflects personal judgement; other sources or instructors may rate hardness differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solution style / terseness
rubrics_metrics.description: The listed USAMO/contest solutions are the author's personal notes and tend to be more terse than other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because these are personal notes rather than 'official' solutions, expect conciseness and possibly less exposition than other published solutions. Use these notes as concise explanations or starting points, and consult other writeups if more detail or pedagogical exposition is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provenance and copyright / non-officiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite being part of the USA team selection process, these are not the 'official' solution files — rather the author's personal notes; internal problems and solutions from the USA(J)MO committee are understood to be copyrighted by MAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume these pages are authoritative official publications; they are reproduced personal materials. The author notes copyright constraints and that internal solution files may not be published elsewhere. For official statements or redistribution permissions, consult the contest organizers or MAA.
